newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore politician sacks lawyers in libel case.
newsitem.headline: Singapore politician sacks lawyers in libel case.

text.p: A Singapore opposition politician facing huge damages for libel fired his lawyers on Monday during a hearing that will decide how much he has to pay, but the court told them to stay on the job.
Lawyers for Tang Liang Hong told the court he had dismissed them by telephone during the lunchtime recess, but they were ordered to stay on as his representatives.
"We no longer have his mandate. It is clear he no longer wants us on board," lawyer Loo Ngan Chor told the court.
Tang fled to Malaysia after losing a bitterly-fought contest in Singapore's general elections in January saying he had received death threats.
He was accused by Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong during the campaign of being a "Chinese chauvinist" who endangered Singapore's multi-racial harmony.
Tang accused Goh, and other leaders of the ruling People's Action Party (PAP) who repeated the charge, of lying. They sued him, saying their integrity had been impugned.
The PAP won 81 of the 83 parliamentary seats in the election.
Tang did not return to Singapore to defend himself in the libel suits, so the court awarded the cases to the PAP leaders in March and is now in the process of deciding how much Tang will have to pay.
Earlier in the libel cases, Tang was ordered to set aside Singapore $11.2 million (US$7.8 million) for damages in the event the libel suits went aginst him.
Davinder Singh, counsel for former prime minister Lee Kuan Yew, called Tang's firing of his lawyers "a ploy cooked up over lunch" to delay the hearing and protested.
"Here is a man who has treated the rules of this court with contempt. Why should he be given any indulgence?" he said.
In the morning session, Tang's lawyers asked for a postponement to allow Tang to bring in a top London lawyer who was not immediately available.
When that was turned down, they said they had "been instructed by our client not to participate in the proceedings". The court ordered them to stay as observers.
Singh alleged that Tang's instructions to his lawyers were part of his attempt to convince the world that he was being persecuted.
"It's a transparent attempt on Mr Tang's part to lay the ground for an interview which he is no doubt going to give to the world's media," he said.
Lee, giving evidence in support of his claim for "exemplary" damages, said he expected Tang to continue attacking the PAP government from abroad.
Tang could be expected to "come out with some denouncement of the whole judicial system" at the end to the hearings, he said.
Tang aimed to portray Singapore as "an oppressive, wicked regime", and to portray him as "a wicked dictator", said Lee, who was Singapore's prime minister for 31 years until he stepped down in 1990.
